title: 3.4. Lists: Mutable Sequences & Memory Allocation
summary: Discover Python lists: ordered, mutable collections. Master positive and negative zero-based indexing, slicing [start:end:step], append(), insert(), and del.
learningObjectives: Construct lists, access elements using zero-based positive and negative indices.
Modify lists in place using append(), insert(), pop(), and the del statement.

sections.heading: 3.4.1 List Anatomy & Zero-Based Indexing
sections.content:
A list is an ordered, mutable sequence of heterogeneous elements enclosed in square brackets [].

• Zero-Based Indexing: The first element is at index 0, the second at 1, etc.
• Negative Indexing: -1 references the last element, -2 the second-to-last, etc.
• Slicing: numbers[1:4] creates a new list from index 1 through index 3 (stop index is exclusive).

recap: Lists are mutable, ordered sequences with flexible slicing and zero-based/negative indexing.
